reason: The cited evidence (E1-E5) comes from a single study on CrFeNiAlSiBx, not AlCrFeNiSi, and shows that B addition causes a lattice constant decrease (E4) and boride formation (E4, E5), but it does not demonstrate reduced lattice distortion or enhanced solid-solution strengthening as a primary mechanism, nor does it compare properties to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi; the claimed improvements in wear and corrosion resistance are stated as research goals in E2, not as demonstrated outcomes for this specific alloy.
premises: Boron addition reduces lattice distortion in AlCrFeNiSi
Boron addition promotes second-phase (boride) formation in AlCrFeNiSi
Boron addition enhances solid-solution strengthening in AlCrFeNiSi
These microstructural changes improve mechanical integrity (hardness, wear, corrosion resistance) relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi
